newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Mubarak and King Hassan discuss Mideast, Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak and King Hassan discuss Mideast, Jerusalem.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Morocco's King Hassan held talks on Friday on the faltering Middle East peace process and on Jerusalem where Israel is planning a new settlement.
After their 70-minute private talks, King Hassan told reporters: "We agreed to convene the Al Qods (Jerusalem) committee as soon as possible." He gave no date.
The 15-member committee, headed by King Hassan, was set up by an Islamic Conference Organisation summit in 1975 with the aim of preventing the city being "judaised" by Israel.
Israel said on Friday it was going ahead with plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews between Arab East Jerusalem and Bethlemen, a move that has fuelled Palestinian action.
King Hassan said Morocco had "no special position" to take with the committee over which it presided administratively. "They (the members) have full responsibility and represent sovereign states."

Mubarak, who arrived earlier on Friday from talks in the United States with President Bill Clinton, made no statement. He was due to dine later with King Hassan and is scheduled to leave for Egypt early on Saturday.

Shortly after Mubarak's arrival, Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told Reuters: "Talks between his majesty King Hassan and President Mubarak will focus on the Arab position on the Middle East peace process, including the situation of Jerusalem.
"They will also discuss other issues in the Arab world."
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said after a visit to Morocco late last month that he and King Hassan had also agreed on the need to hold an urgent meeting of the Al Qods committee.
The committee is made up of Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Guinea, Indonesia, Iran, Niger, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Pakistan, Senegal, Iraq, Syria, Mauritania and the Palestinian Authority.
